bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; emphasized consistent financial performance and operational discipline; no mention of macro headwinds or project risks.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite no formal segment reporting, 9 subsidiaries and 3 JVs indicate deep regional penetration and project diversification across North and Central India, reducing single-project risk.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- States that the "equity commitment [is] comfortably met" against the expanding order book — invested equity of INR 7,158 Million across the eight HAM projects till June 2026.
- Project-level debt as on June 2026 is INR 12,668 Million against total sanctioned debt of INR 32,140 Million, i.e. a large sanctioned-but-undrawn balance at the HAM assets.
- Two HAM assets (Varanasi Kolkata Pkg-10 and Gobindpur Tangi) show no debt drawn as on June 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Well-established infrastructure company with a strong track record executing large-scale EPC and HAM projects, backed by in-house capabilities, a modern equipment base and a skilled workforce enabling efficient project management across all stages.
- Diversified order book of approximately ₹1,01,471 million spanning roads, railways, metro, BESS and energy verticals (Roads/EPC 9.43%, HAM Road 43.72%, Railways 27.84%, Energy vertical 19.02%), reducing dependence on any single segment.
- Strong presence across 14 states, reducing geographic concentration risk and enabling broader opportunity capture.
- Credit ratings reaffirmed at [ICRA]AA- (Positive) for long-term facilities and [ICRA]A1+ for short-term facilities, reflecting strong order book visibility and healthy financial profile.
- Strategic diversification into non-road segments (railways, renewable energy, BESS, T&D) intended to reduce dependence on highways and improve margin stability over the medium term.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Ongoing investigation by the Anti-Corruption Bureau, Patna (matter referenced from January 2026) — The matter was the subject of an Emphasis of Matter by the Statutory Auditors (who otherwise issued an unmodified opinion). Based on management's assessment, legal counsel's opinion and an external firm's review, the Board considers it has no material impact on the FY26 standalone and consolidated financial statements, but the Company continues to extend full cooperation to the investigating agency and further developments are being disclosed to the stock exchanges as they arise.
- Multi-dimensional financial and operational risk exposure — The Company explicitly discloses exposure to market risk, credit risk, liquidity risk, regulatory risk, human resource risk and commodity price risk, overseen by a Board-level Risk Management Committee under a formal Risk Management Policy.
- Rising leverage — The net debt-to-equity ratio increased year-on-year, driven by availment of short-term borrowings for payments to vendors (including related parties), indicating growing reliance on short-term debt to fund working capital.
- Declining profitability and returns — Return on equity and net profit ratio both declined by more than 25% versus the prior year, attributed by the Company directly to a decline in overall operational profitability.
- Deteriorating receivables/collections — The debtors' turnover ratio declined due to higher closing accounts receivable from customers combined with lower revenue during the year, signalling slower cash collection from the order book.
- Cybersecurity and regulatory-compliance risk — Management's Enterprise Risk Management framework placed particular focus on cybersecurity, regulatory compliance and ESG-related risks during the year as emerging threat areas requiring mitigation.
- Geopolitical and input-cost volatility — Global geopolitical disruptions (including the Middle East conflict and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz energy route, alongside elevated tariff risk and trade-policy shifts) create uncertainty for commodity prices, logistics costs and industrial input expenses relevant to the Company's project cost base.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into new states via subsidiaries; potential for JV expansion in highway PPPs; possible entry into greenfield infrastructure projects.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continuing the multi-year transformation from a predominantly roads-focused EPC company into a diversified infrastructure leader spanning roads & highways, railways, metro, renewable energy (solar), BESS and power transmission & distribution.
- Maintaining a bid pipeline of approximately ₹80,000-1,00,000 crore in roads, with growing exposure to rail, transmission and energy, using presence across EPC, HAM and BOQ models to participate across procurement cycles.
- Accelerating monetisation of HAM assets to reduce debt and support capital recycling, moving the energy vertical from commitment to active execution.
- Maintaining a sustainable balance sheet through disciplined bidding, operational efficiency, prudent capital allocation and strong cash flow management, prioritising profitable growth over pure scale.
- Widening the client base beyond government counterparties to include private developers (e.g. Welspun for the Pune-Shirur highway).
- Exploring adjacent opportunities in building construction and expansion of existing infrastructure, similar to the Narol and Urban Extension Road (UER) projects.
- Enhancing bottom-line performance through digital transformation and process optimisation, translating operational excellence into stakeholder returns.
- The Board recommended a final dividend to shareholders for FY 2025-26 (a per-share amount, not reproduced here), consistent with a stated Dividend Distribution Policy, while continuing to prioritise reinvestment of capital into project execution and growth areas (HAM, solar, BESS, transmission) alongside balance-sheet discipline.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Growth capex is concentrated in HAM (Hybrid Annuity Model) equity funding, solar commissioning and BESS build-out rather than physical plant additions. Against a total estimated equity requirement of approximately ₹1,903 crore across 11 HAM projects, ₹1,210 crore had already been infused as of 31 March 2026, with the balance expected to be phased over the next three financial years in line with project execution. The renewable energy (solar) portfolio surpassed approximately 96% financial completion, with a substantial number of plants already commissioned and generating revenue; the majority of pending debt disbursements are expected upon project commissioning in FY 2026-27. The BESS business is progressing execution across projects aggregating 735 MW / 1,470 MWh, expected to generate stable, annuity-like revenues once commissioned. As part of its ongoing HAM asset monetisation strategy, the Company completed the transfer of its 100% stake in four HAM assets during FY26 and the subsequent months, generating cash inflows for capital recycling; monetisation of the remaining identified HAM assets is expected to further strengthen the balance sheet and support future expansion. Standalone gross debt stood at ₹1,627 crore as of 31 March 2026, comprising working capital borrowings, NCDs and project-related debt, with management expecting project commissioning, HAM monetisation proceeds, solar debt drawdowns and improving operating cash flows to strengthen the leverage profile over coming quarters.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government capital expenditure on infrastructure has increased sixfold over the past decade, budgeted at ₹12.20 lakh crore for FY 2026-27, making infrastructure a structural rather than cyclical policy priority.
- NHAI's awarding pace slowed significantly in FY 2025-26 as the government recalibrated project structuring, deferring awards across HAM, EPC and BOT modes without reducing the underlying pipeline.
- A record ₹2.78 lakh crore was allocated to railways in FY27, with award activity in this segment more consistent than roads, spanning station redevelopment, freight corridors and metro expansion.
- Battery storage has moved from policy ambition to active procurement, with utilities now signing binding long-term agreements with developers as India's renewable energy targets require storage at scale.
- India's transmission network requires significant expansion to absorb growing renewable energy generation, creating a pipeline of long-tenure concession projects with predictable long-term revenue.
- FY26 saw sector-wide margin and execution pressure driven by input-cost inflation from geopolitical disruption in West Asia, compounded by appointed-date delays and a slowdown in order awards.
- Diversification is reducing dependence on highways: non-road segments now account for a rising share of the order book (railways 27.84%, energy vertical/BESS 19.02%), with project wins in FY26 across metro, transmission and BESS demonstrating execution of the diversification strategy.
- Entry into BESS and transmission aligns the Company with high-growth segments linked to India's energy transition, where long-term demand visibility is strong; the transmission sector alone is expected to see capital deployment of ₹9.16 lakh crore.
- Asset monetisation (five HAM assets) is expected to unlock capital and improve liquidity, enabling redeployment into new projects without significant balance-sheet stress and supporting a more asset-light growth approach.
- Sustained government capex in roads, railways and energy, and participation across EPC, HAM and emerging segments, is expected to continue providing a strong pipeline of projects and order inflows.
- Order book stood at ₹1,01,470-1,01,471 million as of FY 2025-26, down from ₹1,52,812 million in FY 2024-25, with a healthy mix of government (94.00%) and private (6.00%) projects.
- Order book (post new orders, FY 2026-27) is stated at approximately ₹1,57,386 million.
- Total order inflows for FY 2025-26 reached ₹45,042.51 million (excluding GST), including ₹14,232 million from the strategic expansion into railway, metro and renewable energy sectors; this figure includes ₹41,420.90 million in orders removed from the order book due to execution uncertainty following a lack of clarification from the Authority.
- Ten ongoing railway and metro projects are in the order book, with the DMRC project at 99.4% completion and the New Delhi Railway Station in full execution, described as building credentials for larger bids ahead.
- Roads and highways continue to account for the largest share of the order book; FY26 additions include the Pune-Shirur EPC project from private developer Welspun and the Capital Region Ring Road Package III HAM project in Odisha.
- Energy vertical (solar, BESS and T&D) together now account for approximately 19% of the order book.
- The Company maintains a bid pipeline of approximately ₹80,000 to ₹1,00,000 crore in roads, with growing exposure to rail, transmission and energy.

drhp.business: HGIEL provides integrated engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) services and undertakes projects under the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM), with operations spanning transportation, renewable energy and emerging areas such as BESS and power transmission. It has recently entered the power transmission and distribution (T&D) segment, securing its first interstate transmission project under the Eastern Region Generation Scheme. Its customers are Central and State Government agencies, statutory authorities and private sector enterprises, with no export or international operations.

risks.risk: Multi-dimensional financial and operational risk exposure

risks.note: The net debt-to-equity ratio increased year-on-year, driven by availment of short-term borrowings for payments to vendors (including related parties), indicating growing reliance on short-term debt to fund working capital.
Return on equity and net profit ratio both declined by more than 25% versus the prior year, attributed by the Company directly to a decline in overall operational profitability.
The debtors' turnover ratio declined due to higher closing accounts receivable from customers combined with lower revenue during the year, signalling slower cash collection from the order book.
Management's Enterprise Risk Management framework placed particular focus on cybersecurity, regulatory compliance and ESG-related risks during the year as emerging threat areas requiring mitigation.

Global geopolitical disruptions (including the Middle East conflict and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz energy route, alongside elevated tariff risk and trade-policy shifts) create uncertainty for commodity prices, logistics costs and industrial input expenses relevant to the Company's project cost base.
